jurisdiction.name: Armenia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Armenia has no standalone AI law and no adopted national AI strategy; the 2021-2025 digitalisation strategy contained a few AI actions, and a high-tech sector strategy for 2026-2033 with AI as a priority was not confirmed as adopted. AI governance runs through the Ministry of High-Tech Industry, renamed in 2026 to include Artificial Intelligence, a 2025 state programme giving AI innovators free high-performance computing, 2026 relief for AI data-centre construction, and a 2026 amendment to the audiovisual media law requiring AI-generated content to be labelled. Draft Criminal Code amendments on AI-generated material were put to consultation in 2025, the government approved signing the Council of Europe AI Convention in December 2024, and the 2015 data protection law applies.
lead_institutions: Ministry of High-Tech Industry and Artificial Intelligence
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The high-tech sector strategy is listed as a lead. Not yet verified from the official text: the adoption of the high-tech sector strategy and any AI guidance from the data protection agency.

instruments.current_status: In force since 1 July 2015 (art. 28), amended several times; ARLIS shows the consolidated version in force from 15 August 2026. Published in the Official Bulletin (HHPT 2015.06.18/35(1124), art. 462). It contains no AI-specific provisions; the decision-making rule in art. 16 is the closest provision to automated-decision rules.
instruments.summary: Armenia's general data protection law (HO-49-N, adopted 18 May 2015), governing the processing of personal data by public bodies and private persons, including automated processing, and setting principles of legality, proportionality, accuracy and minimal involvement of data subjects. Article 16 prohibits taking decisions with legal effects for a data subject on the basis of personal-data processing except with the subject's consent or where a law provides, and Article 13 sets special rules for biometric data. It establishes the authorised body for personal data protection (the Personal Data Protection Agency) with supervisory and sanctioning powers.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law; governs personal data used to train and run AI systems and restricts decisions with legal effect based on personal-data processing (art. 16).

AI appears only in a few actions, such as using AI (natural language processing) in the digital document-management system to support decision-making and supporting AI and cybersecurity research projects and demo labs; it has no dedicated AI pillar.

instruments.current_status: Adopted 25 December 2025, officially published 26 December 2025, in force from 27 December 2025; the programme runs in 2026. A draft amending it (e-draft project 10424, July 2026) and a related draft procedure for public authorities' access to AI computing (e-draft 10426) were in consultation in 2026.
instruments.summary: Government decision N 1966-N of 25 December 2025, adopted under the Law on State Support to the High-Tech Sector, approving a 2026 pilot programme that gives AI innovators 100% subsidised (free) access to high-performance computing (CPU/GPU cloud) resources. The Ministry of High-Tech Industry implements it and is authorised to conclude a subsidy agreement with Amazon Web Services, with a 2026 state-budget ceiling of AMD 400 million; the annex sets eligibility and the application procedure.

instruments.english_title: Law amending the Law on Audiovisual Media (mandatory labelling of AI-generated synthetic content, HO-134-N)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly of the Republic of Armenia
instruments.current_status: Adopted 7 April 2026, signed and officially published 18 April 2026, in force 28 April 2026 (tenth day after publication). The Ministry of High-Tech Industry's draft was on e-draft.am (project 9898, consultation 13-28 March 2026).
instruments.summary: Law HO-134-N (adopted 7 April 2026) adds a definition of 'synthetic content' created or altered with generative AI, machine learning or other digital technologies and a new article 9.1 requiring audiovisual media service providers to label such content clearly ('Created by AI' for generative-AI content, 'Subjected to digital processing' for other digitally altered content). It sets how labels must appear in video, audio and images, allows lighter labelling for fiction, humour and educational programmes, empowers the regulator to set detailed requirements, and adds a fine of 300 times the minimum wage for breaches (art. 57).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: AI-specific labelling obligation for synthetic (AI-generated) content in broadcast media.

instruments.summary: Government draft law amending the 2021 Criminal Code, published for public consultation on e-draft.am. Among child-protection and online-harassment changes, it would add as an aggravating element of art. 258 (hooliganism-type offences) the use of AI-generated material that defames, threatens violence or contains sexual propositions, and extend art. 300(5) to imitated material 'including material created by artificial intelligence'.
